text: Malignant bone tumors can result in physical disability, which has a significant impact on the quality of patients’ survival. Additionally, patients often experience high levels of psychological distress. The subjective well-being of patients with bone tumors is low, and this low level of well-being is the direct cause of the accumulation of negative emotions and misanthropy in patients.
source_label: Change trajectory of dyadic coping and subjective well-being in patients with malignant bone tumors based on cross-lagged panel model and latent growth model: a longitudinal study
